text: Israel is a luxuriant vine that yields his fruit for himself. The more his fruit increased, the more altars he built; the richer his land became, the finer he made his sacred pillars.

versions.text: Israel is a luxuriant vine that yields its fruit for itself. The more his fruit increased, the more altars he built; the richer his land became, the finer he made his sacred pillars.
versions.explanation: The verse switches from "its fruit for itself" to "his fruit ... he built ... his land," which is jarring when read aloud. Keeping one pronoun set (masculine, as in the Hebrew) makes the rhythm consistent.

text: Their heart is divided, and now they must bear their guilt. He will break down their altars and destroy their sacred pillars.
For now they will say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD—and what could a king do for us anyway?"

versions.text: Then they will say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD—and what could a king do for us anyway?"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew כִּי עַתָּה carries the sense "for now / indeed now," linking this verse to the judgment just announced. "Then" loses that connective force.

text: They speak empty words, swear false oaths, and make covenants; so judgment springs up like a poisonous weed among the furrows of the field.
The inhabitants of Samaria tremble for the calves of Beth Aven. Its people mourn over it, and its idol priests wail over it, over its glory, for it has been carried away from them.

versions.text: The inhabitants of Samaria tremble for the calf of Beth Aven. Its people mourn over it, and its priests wail over it, over its glory, for it has been carried away from them.
versions.explanation: עֶגְלוֹת is plural ("calves"), and כְּמָרִים is a distinct term for idolatrous priests, not the ordinary word for priests; making this explicit avoids the impression that legitimate priests are meant.

text: The idol itself will be carried off to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be put to shame, and Israel disgraced by its own counsel.
Samaria is destroyed; her king is like a twig adrift on the water.
The high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be laid waste. Thorns and thistles will grow over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, "Cover us!" and to the hills, "Fall on us!"
Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel; there they have taken their stand. Will not war overtake them in Gibeah, the sons of iniquity?
When I please, I will discipline them; nations will be gathered against them, to bind them for their double guilt.
Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, but I will put a yoke on her fair neck. I will harness Ephraim; Judah must plow, and Jacob must break up the ground.
Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap the harvest of mercy. Break up your fallow ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and rains righteousness upon you.
But you have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you trusted in your own way, in the multitude of your warriors,

the roar of battle will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.

versions.text: the roar of battle will rise against your people, and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.
versions.explanation: בְּעַמֶּךָ means "among/in your people" — the tumult arises within Israel itself. "Against your people" shifts the sense to an external attacker.

text: So it will be done to you, Bethel, because of your great wickedness. At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
